# Constructed archive custody review checkpoint

This is independent engineering evidence from fabricated CSV bytes, fabricated exact feature vectors, and fixed synthetic source-role assignments. No actual archived formula, feature vector, target cell, or scientific allocation was read or drawn. Main source and dependency files were read. All reviewer writes remain in this scratch review directory.

The independent fixture has the public 1,545-row / 314-condition-row shape, 75 source groups, and 35 / 20 / 20 development / calibration / evaluation roles. Eligible rows occupy alternating original ordinals. Ineligible cells contain non-UTF-8 target canaries, and an unrelated quoted field contains embedded line endings. Neither is a recorded experiment.

## Preserved findings

1. Initial immutable-case checks exposed two feature-to-input linkage failures: a dataclass replacement could reuse the copied authority, and a nested input snapshot remained mutable. The author added issued-case identity, deep immutable snapshots, and reconstruction checks before input use. Both original regressions subsequently passed.
2. The first broad run stopped before target decode because a newly immutable route identity was passed to a strict dictionary-only store API. The author added an explicit ordinary-dictionary copy at that boundary. The failed run remains available.
3. The second broad run executed 15 checks in 118.091 seconds. Fourteen passed. A corrupt rank-file check raised while the driver attempted to construct its unavailable result: result issuance called store verification again on the already detected corrupt prefix. The source did stop all reserved decoding. The author proposed separating recorded result identity from mandatory persisted-byte verification before public projection. This repair has not yet been independently rerun at this checkpoint.

The second run also passed a fresh-process replay of the same fabricated fixed roles, preserving all eight scientific stage digests, allocation identity, and kernel evaluation identity. It drew no scientific entropy and is not an independent scientific sample. A separate completed store review tests byte-preserving original-allocation import; these two controls should not be conflated.

## Scope and remaining gate

The tested workflow covers one source capture, complete source-size/MD5/SHA checks before framing, framing before numeric decoding, fixed development and rank boundaries, all 960 actual policy ledgers, literal secondary membership restrictions, inadequacy before model/reserved access, all-unknown endpoints with unavailable components, exact source/feature linkage, and preserved failure prefixes. Registration authentication, operating-system isolation, launcher validation, and public projection have separate owners. Source-free registration tests here establish rejection and call wiring only.

The v2 run bound custody, driver, flow, kernel, helper, and reviewer hashes before and after; those remained stable. An unrelated launcher file changed during the run, so the broad all-script inventory explicitly records that change instead of claiming every inventoried file was frozen. A final source-bound receipt is pending the narrow failure-path repair and final independent run.

No engineering pass, digest equality, or formal theorem establishes physical accuracy, chemical independence, a sound sampling premise, or empirical recommendation superiority.

## Final reviewed core checkpoint

The repaired driver `993470740a163f28ee0a9e247603d80b52b5045c8d7943f33fd86075d6cf7df4` passed all 18 independent checks in 132.487 seconds. All 26 inventoried source/specification/test hashes were identical before and after the run; `PYTHONPATH` was removed. Both original case regressions, the corrupt-prefix unavailable return and validation rejection, and invalid/stale plan checks before future-vault access passed. The exact run, source identities, failure history, scope and remaining integration gates are recorded in `archive-custody-independent-review-v1.json`.

There is no remaining blocker in this reviewed core scope. Registration, supervision, launcher and public bridge remain separately reviewed boundaries; this checkpoint is not permission to treat an unexecuted actual study as passed. Temporary test data deliberately lives beneath this ignored review lane. A promoted test-layout change needs its own rerun.
